# Bar (horizontal)

Contents: [Use cases](#use-cases), [Design](#design), [Chart IDs](#chart-ids), [Minimal spec](#minimal-spec), [Data](#data), [Options](#options), [Annotations](#annotations), [Dense value labels](#dense-value-labels), [Sizing](#sizing), [Fixtures](#fixtures).

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-reference.mjs from the boardplot describe, list and fixtures payloads. -->

Horizontal item comparison — grouped, stacked, or 100%-stacked rows with direct labels. Type `bar`.

## Use cases

- Ranking items
- Tornado or football-field ranges
- Values with long category names

## Design

**Message:** How items rank or compare on one measure.

**Use when:** Categories without a natural order, or names too long to fit under a column.

**Not when:** The categories are periods (column or line); a few parts of one whole (pie or waffle); two measures per item (dot or butterfly).

### design-bar-sort

Sort unordered bars by value, largest first, so the ranking reads from the top. Render checks this rule and returns the warning `design-bar-sort` with severity `advice`. A `fix` patch is included only when it can apply to the input as sent; otherwise follow `suggest`, for example when waterfall items come from rows.

### design-bar-one-colour

Give one measure one colour and mark only the item the title names with options.highlight; a colour per bar is a code the reader must learn. This rule needs the author's judgment; render does not check it.

### design-bar-many

Show at most 15 bars; fold the tail into one Others bar so the items that matter stay readable. Render checks this rule and returns the warning `design-bar-many` with severity `advice`. A `fix` patch is included only when it can apply to the input as sent; otherwise follow `suggest`, for example when waterfall items come from rows.

### design-bar-zero

Start the value axis at zero: a bar's length is its value, so a cut axis overstates the differences. This rule needs the author's judgment; render does not check it.

### design-bar-stack-limit

Keep a stacked bar to about five segments: only the first segment and the total share a baseline, so the middle segments are hard to compare. This rule needs the author's judgment; render does not check it.

### design-bar-title

Write the finding in the title, such as "North sells 30% more than South", not the name of the measure. This rule needs the author's judgment; render does not check it.

## Chart IDs

- `bar.grouped`: fixture `axis-break`
- `bar.stacked`: fixture `stacked-net-line-horizontal`
- `bar.stacked100`: fixture `ai-products-by-region`
- `bar.football-field`: fixture `valuation-football-field`
- `bar.tornado`: fixture `dcf-npv-sensitivity`

## Minimal spec

```json
{
  "type": "bar",
  "data": {
    "categories": [{ "id": "north", "label": "North" }, { "id": "south", "label": "South" }],
    "series": [{ "id": "revenue", "label": "Revenue", "values": [120, 90] }]
  },
  "options": { "unit": "$k", "title": "North revenue exceeds South by $30k", "source": "Illustrative data" }
}
```

## Data

A `cell` is a number, null or a value object; see [Value cell](options.md#value-cell).

| Path | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| valueKind | string |  | Default valueKind for all series. One of `'fraction'`. |
| categories | array | yes | Ordered categories defining the displayed rows and positional value alignment. |
| categories[].id | string | yes | Category identity used to match keyed values and annotation anchors. |
| categories[].label | string |  | Displayed category name; defaults to the category id and supports line breaks. A date id or `date` without a label prints a short date such as '4 Sep'. |
| categories[].date | string |  | ISO 8601 category date, yyyy-mm-dd; strictly increasing dates permit date-axis promotion where supported. |
| categories[].total100 | number |  | Authored quantity represented by 100%; otherwise percentage variants derive their basis from the category values. |
| categories[].gapAfter | boolean \| number |  | Extra band-step fractions after this category; true defaults to 0.5. |
| categories[].breakAfter | boolean |  | Category axis break after this category: a gap of at least half a band step with the straight break glyph on the category baseline. Series connectors and net-line steps do not cross it. |
| categories[].footnote | integer |  | 1-based reference into options.footnotes. The number is drawn beside this category label as the reference mark, and the note it points at keeps that number; a reference to no note draws nothing and warns, and notes the engine derives print unnumbered. |
| categories[].partial | boolean |  | Period still running, such as the current week. Bars and segments on it are hatched and line markers on it are hollow; marks keep their positions. A drawn key names the running category once as "<label> to date". With no such key, the frame adds that note. |
| series | array | yes | Series supplying values for each category, with optional reference series for comparisons. |
| series[].valueKind | string |  | Multiply numbers by 100 into pct cells; explicit pct cells stay in percent units. One of `'fraction'`. |
| series[].id | string | yes | Series identity used by keyed options, annotations and legend entries. |
| series[].label | string |  | Displayed series name; defaults to the series id. |
| series[].values | (cell \| { categoryId, value: cell })[] | yes | Values in category order, or keyed entries pairing a categoryId with its value. |
| series[].scenario | string |  | AC, PY, PL, FC (or ACT, BUD, FCST). Controls scenario labels and paint conventions. |
| series[].direction | string |  | Whether increases are favorable; defaults to higherIsBetter for directional comparisons. One of `'higherIsBetter'`, `'lowerIsBetter'`. |
| series[].role | string |  | Data series or comparison-only reference series; references are excluded from the main plotted data. One of `'data'`, `'reference'`. |
| series[].colorRole | string |  | Theme color role used for this series when no explicit fill takes precedence. One of good, bad, warn, neutral, neutralLight, highlight, total, others; series-N for step N of the theme ramp, 1-based (series-2 is color.series[1]); or status-<key> for a theme status colour. A hex colour goes in fill. |
| series[].fill | string |  | Explicit CSS fill color for this series; remains authored across theme changes. |
| series[].unit | string |  | Unit of this series' values, used to check shared-scale compatibility. Without a format example, a $k, $m, k or m unit prints its labels whole from 100 up, in place of options.unit. |
| series[].format | string |  | Format-by-example for this series' labels, for example 1,234 or 1.2%. Overrides options.format; a cell format overrides it. |

## Options

| Path | Type | Values | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| labelDensity | string | `'full'`, `'smart'`, `'minimal'` |  | Value-label density. Default 'smart': every value stays eligible. A chart with more than 12 categories, or with most labels wider than the band, ranks the first, last, highest and lowest value (ties: the first) first. The other values then use only their natural seat beside the mark; with none free they are drawn nowhere and left out of the note. Those four may take one step, and the note names any that finds no seat. A smaller chart keeps every value on the bounded one-step rule and names any that finds no seat. 'full' treats all values alike and names every one that finds no seat. 'minimal' also applies the shared priority gate. Seats stay inside the plot band and one step from the natural seat. All values remain in reading records. When valueLabels is set, it wins: labelDensity is not read for the value labels. |
| legend | string \| object | `'top'`, `'bottom'`, `'none'`, `'auto'` (or another value of its type) |  | Key position. Multiple series get a key by default unless visible direct labels name them all. 'none' hides the key and warns if names are missing. Subtitle and footnote mentions do not replace the key. |
| valueAxis.break | false \| object | `false` (or another value of its type) |  | No break by default or with false. Set { from, to, style? } for a straight value-axis break; the omitted span collapses to a fixed 12px gap when valid. Automatic placement is supported only by waterfall and pvm. |
| axisTitles | object |  |  | Title of the value axis when valueAxis.show draws it: in the tick-label row, ending at the right end of the axis past the last tick label or short of the first tick label, and in a row of its own under the ticks only when neither side has room. A theme with valueAxis.titles derives 'Measure, unit' from subtitle.measure and a unit the drawn subtitle does not print, when none is authored. |
| axisTitles.primary | string |  |  | 'Measure, unit' title of the value axis, e.g. 'Margin, %'. |
| valueLabels | string | `'none'`, `'last'`, `'ends'`, `'extremes'`, `'all'` |  | Which values print, with line's choices: 'none', 'last', 'ends' (first and last), 'extremes' (first, last, highest and lowest; a tie takes the first) or 'all', chosen per series over the categories in their drawn order. Unset (default): every value is eligible and labelDensity decides. When set, valueLabels wins over labelDensity: each chosen value takes the one-step rule of 'full', and one with no seat is named in the note. A value not chosen is unlabelled by choice: the note does not name it, and the value axis is drawn so it stays readable (all modes but 'all'; valueAxis.show false turns it off). Authored cell labels print in every mode. Grouped only: a stack has no single value per category, so stacked, stacked100, football-field and tornado refuse every mode but 'all' with value-labels-variant. Example: a ranking of 12 bars with 'extremes' prints the top, bottom, highest and lowest value. |
| variant | string | `'grouped'`, `'stacked'`, `'stacked100'`, `'football-field'`, `'tornado'` | `'grouped'` | Horizontal arrangement; grouped by default. Stacked100 normalizes category totals; football-field shows ranges and tornado compares low/high driver cases. |
| sharesOfOneWhole | boolean |  |  | true declares every stacked series a share of the same whole, such as channel shares of all orders: the stack then has a total, and percent series warn non-additive-stack only where a category adds to more than 100. Stacked and stacked100 only; refused on other variants. |
| baseValue | number \| object |  |  | Tornado base-case output metric; the vertical spine every swing is measured against. Required for variant 'tornado'. |
| baseValue.value | number |  |  | Base-case output value used as the tornado comparison spine. |
| baseValue.label | string |  |  | Label naming the tornado base case. |
| tornado | object |  |  | Tornado case identity. Two named series, not one range cell: a range normalizes low>high away and would destroy an inverse driver's case colouring. |
| tornado.low | string |  |  | Series carrying the output metric with this driver at its LOW input. |
| tornado.high | string |  |  | Series carrying the output metric with this driver at its HIGH input. |
| currentValue | number \| object |  |  | Football-field vertical current-value marker; number shorthand uses an automatic label. |
| currentValue.value | number |  |  | Current output value marked across the football-field ranges. |
| currentValue.label | string |  |  | Authored label for the football-field current-value marker. |
| methodNote | boolean |  |  | Default false. true adds the method footnotes: the mid-point tick of a football-field range, drawn only with its note, and the one-at-a-time contract of a tornado. Hatched tornado bars and drivers that could not be drawn are required for interpretation and print regardless. |
| grandTotalLabels | boolean |  |  | Show category stack-total labels in addition to segment labels; default on for the stacked variant and off for stacked100, where every bar would end on the same share. true keeps the absolute total on a 100% stack. |
| referenceStyle | string | `'tick'`, `'line'`, `'marker'` | `'tick'` | Reference-series mark style; defaults to tick. Line references use a 1.25px stroke. |
| referenceTick | object |  |  | Weight and ink of the reference tick, read under referenceStyle 'tick' only: the dotted 'line' uses stroke.rule and the 'marker' its neutral dot. A prior-year mark that must stand out is { width: 2, color: 'highlight' }. |
| referenceTick.width | number |  |  | Stroke width of the tick in px; default 1.6. |
| referenceTick.color | string | `'ink'`, `'highlight'` |  | Ink of the tick; default 'ink'. 'highlight' is the accent for the one mark the reader should find first. |
| signColor | boolean |  |  | Paint each bar good/bad/neutral by sign(value) × series.direction (zero is neutral), as on column. Under series.direction 'lowerIsBetter' the encoding inverts, positives paint bad and negatives good, so the chart brings its own legend naming the polarity in words; suppressing it with legend 'none' is reported as legend-suppressed-encoding. colorblindSafe swaps the pair for the colour-vision-safe one. Requires variant 'grouped' with exactly one data-role series; anything else is refused with sign-color-unsupported. Cells with an explicit fill, a highlight, or the topN 'Others' bucket keep their own paint and report sign-color-overridden. |
| netLine | boolean \| object |  |  | Per-category ticks at a cumulative boundary of stacked bars; connectors default to false. |
| netLine.seriesId | string |  |  | Series whose cumulative boundary receives a tick; omitted uses the positive stack end. |
| netLine.connectors | boolean |  |  | Must remain false for bars because structural category axes carry no sequence. |
| averageMarker | boolean \| object |  |  | Computed dashed average rule with a solver-placed Ø label. |
| averageMarker.scope | string \| array | `'all'` (or another value of its type) |  | Series included in the computed average; defaults to 'all'. |
| connectors | boolean \| object |  |  | Connect matching series boundaries between adjacent stacked bars. |
| connectors.style | string | `'line'`, `'dashed'` |  | Connector stroke: solid 'line' (default) or 'dashed', matching the waterfall bridge's dash. |
| connectors.scope | string \| array | `'all'` (or another value of its type) |  | Series boundaries to connect; defaults to 'all'. |

Plus the [shared options](options.md). This type does not accept `categoryLabels`, `valueAxis.tickStep`, `valueAxis.log`, `valueAxis.reverse`, `categoryAxis`, `secondaryAxis`, `ribbons`.

## Annotations

An annotation anchor is a category or item id string, or an object with categoryId plus optional seriesId, segmentId and edge (start, end, total); pointId addresses a scatter point. Category anchors, including from/to, take category ids, not category labels.

| Kind | Purpose | Required | Anchors | Optional fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| valueLine | Draws a reference line at an authored value or an engine-computed mean, with optional tolerance shading and attainment fill between the line and resolved actuals. |  | from: categoryId (optional); to: categoryId (optional) | value: number \| 'mean', default mean. A number draws the line there; mean has the engine compute it. valueKind: 'fraction'. Multiply a numeric value and its tolerance by 100 before layout: 0.35 draws at 35%. Independent of data.valueKind. Omit it for values already in percent points; not valid with mean. label: string \| false. Name plus value; ${value} sets its position. A number already in the name is kept once. false hides it. tolerance: number \| { low, high }. A number shades that distance on both sides of the line; low and high shade an authored corridor. attainment: boolean \| { seriesId, direction }. Shades each category between its actual and the line. | No anchor is required. Value defaults to mean. Scoped means are line-only: seriesId and paired from/to compute a primary-axis mean and limit its stroke to those bands; other types refuse scope fields for a mean. Numeric values cannot use scope fields except as a category clip with tolerance or attainment. A secondary-axis line needs an acknowledged secondary scale and an explicit numeric value. Optional tolerance shades a value-axis band; optional attainment fills between the line and resolved actuals. |
| indicator100 | Maps 100 through the chart's value scale and draws a side tick with a 100% label. |  |  | side: left \| right, default left. Side of the plot the 100% mark sits on. | No anchor is required. The chart needs a value scale that can represent 100. |
| callout | Places authored free text at an anchored data element, routing a leader when displaced and honoring the preferred side. | at, text | at: AnchorRef | preferSide: left \| right \| above \| below. Side the solver tries first; the label keeps a leader when it moves. headline: string. A bold first line over the text, which then prints in plain type; ${value} in it prints the anchored value from the data. Example: "headline": "${value}", "text": "Peak in handheld-loom demand" prints 153 in bold over the words. arrow: boolean, default false. A thin arrow from the text to the anchored point; the first line sits level with the point, right or left of it, where there is room. Not with icon or status. Example: "arrow": true. | Drawn reference series accept anchors. |
| note | Places authored text at an anchored data element through collision avoidance, with an optional icon or status chip. | at, text | at: AnchorRef |  | Drawn reference series accept anchors. |
| delta | Computes the signed difference between an anchored value and another anchor or literal, then places a collision-managed label at the first anchor. | at, vs | at: AnchorRef; vs: AnchorRef \| number |  | Drawn reference series accept anchors. |
| abs | Reads the anchored data value and places its formatted absolute value in a collision-managed label. | at | at: AnchorRef |  | Drawn reference series accept anchors. |
| diff | Draws a level-difference arrow between two anchors and computes either percent change or their signed value difference. | from, to | from: AnchorRef; to: AnchorRef | mode: relative \| absolute \| reversed, default relative. relative prints the percent change from 'from' to 'to', reversed the change from 'to' to 'from', absolute the value difference. | Mode defaults to relative. Relative and reversed changes need a nonzero base; negative bases use its absolute magnitude and emit a warning. Absolute mode reports the raw value difference. A hidden label removes its arm. Drawn reference series accept anchors. |
| band | Draws an inclusive category span as a shaded band or bracket, or a value-axis plan corridor, tolerance band or attainment fill, with a collision-managed label. |  | from: categoryId (optional); to: categoryId (optional) |  | Era shade/bracket needs inclusive category IDs. Corridor and tolerance use finite low/high on the value scale, with optional from/to as a category clip. Attainment needs a plan value and shades each resolved actual; missing cells are skipped. Divider applies only to bracket bands. Scenario AC/PY/PL/FC paints a plan corridor (default PL). |
| cagr | Draws a growth arrow between two anchored points and computes the compound annual growth rate from their values and ISO-date span. |  | from: AnchorRef (optional); to: AnchorRef (optional) | suffix: string, default 'p.a.'. Text after the rate. period: boolean. Print the period before the rate from the anchors' category labels, '2014–2019: +5.8% p.a.'. Default true when the chart carries two or more CAGRs, so nested brackets are told apart by their text, false otherwise. An arrow's ends show its span, so an arrow prints the rate alone unless period is true. shape: bracket \| arrow, default bracket. arrow draws one straight arrow over the marks with the rate in an oval on it, lifted until it clears them. Where no straight line clears the chart, a stack's inner layer is the anchor or the chart lays comparisons out itself, it draws the bracket and warns cagr-arrow-no-room. | Omitted endpoints span the first to the last category, or the first to the last total on a waterfall. Resolved endpoints need a positive date interval from ISO dates or year-bearing labels and a positive start value; an end of zero reads -100%, and a start at or below zero or a negative end omits the rate and warns cagr-undefined. On a continuous time axis the years are the exact span between the two readings. An anchor on one series of several (seriesId, or a line category, which reads the first drawn series) names that series in the label, "Product B +10.1% p.a.", and the arm runs from that series' segment or point. In text, ${value} prints the rate with its suffix, so "CAGR 2014–2019: ${value}" keeps the computed number. Drawn reference series accept anchors. |

## Dense value labels

The default `labelDensity: 'smart'` keeps every value eligible. In a chart with more than 12 categories, or with most labels wider than the band, the first, last, highest and lowest values (ties: the first) take their seats first, and the note names any of them that finds none. A smaller chart keeps every value on the one-step rule and names any that finds no seat. Other values use only their natural seat beside the mark, and are dropped without a note entry when it is taken. Stacked bars apply this rule to totals. Use `labelDensity: 'full'` to treat all values alike and name every value without a seat. Reading records keep every value.

## Sizing

Floor 280 × 28 px; fit `content`.

Below the floor a render is refused with `size-below-floor` and the pixels it needs. `measure` returns the natural and comfortable size for a given spec; see [Sizing in the manual](../manual.md#sizing).
